quote: Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.
author: Warren Buffett
note: A great company can still be a poor investment if you overpay. Separate the business from the price.

quote: Don't look for the needle in the haystack. Just buy the haystack!
author: John C. Bogle
note: The founder of Vanguard built the index fund on one idea: owning the whole market beats trying to find the winners.

quote: The key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
author: Peter Lynch
note: Most long-term returns are lost not in crashes, but in selling during them.

quote: Someone's sitting in the shade today because someone planted a tree a long time ago.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Compounding rewards patience. The best time to start was years ago; the next best is today.

quote: Time is your friend; impulse is your enemy.
author: John C. Bogle
note: Impulsive trades feel productive. Time in a sensible portfolio is what compounds.

quote: In the short run, the market is a voting machine but in the long run, it is a weighing machine.
author: Benjamin Graham
note: Sentiment moves prices day to day. Earnings and cash flows decide where they settle.

quote: Our favorite holding period is forever.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Buy businesses you would be happy to own for decades, and let compounding do the work.

quote: Know what you own, and know why you own it.
author: Peter Lynch
note: If you can't explain a holding in two lines, you won't know what to do when it falls.

quote: The stock market is filled with individuals who know the price of everything, but the value of nothing.
author: Philip Fisher
note: Price is a number on a screen. Value comes from the business behind it.

quote: It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Quality compounds. Cheap stocks are often cheap for a reason.

quote: The big money is not in the buying or the selling, but in the waiting.
author: Charlie Munger
note: Activity is overrated. The fortune is made by holding good investments for long periods.

quote: Investing should be more like watching paint dry or watching grass grow.
author: Paul Samuelson
note: If you want excitement, go to Las Vegas. Wealth building is meant to be boring.

quote: Wide diversification is only required when investors do not understand what they are doing.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Buffett's point is about expertise. For most investors who aren't full-time analysts, his advice is the opposite: own a low-cost index fund.

quote: The four most dangerous words in investing are: this time it's different.
author: Sir John Templeton
note: Every bubble has a story about why old rules no longer apply. They usually still do.

quote: Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Crowd emotion creates the best and worst prices. Discipline means acting against it.

quote: Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections than has been lost in corrections themselves.
author: Peter Lynch
note: Waiting for the perfect dip usually costs more than the dip itself.

quote: The investor's chief problem, and even his worst enemy, is likely to be himself.
author: Benjamin Graham
note: Markets don't ruin most investors. Their own behaviour does.

quote: Risk comes from not knowing what you're doing.
author: Warren Buffett
note: Understanding what you own, and why, is the cheapest form of risk management.

quote: Bull markets are born on pessimism, grow on skepticism, mature on optimism, and die on euphoria.
author: Sir John Templeton
note: The mood of the crowd tells you where you are in the cycle.

quote: The first rule of compounding: never interrupt it unnecessarily.
author: Charlie Munger
note: Every exit resets the clock that compounding depends on.
